subject: maths
title: Numbers to 20 - Odd, Even, Order and Money

steps.title: Partners, positions and coins

options.label: Seven socks make three pairs and one left over. Is seven odd or even?
Ali finishes first, Mona second and Omar third. Who is in second position?
One pound is one hundred piastres. Which coin is worth the most?

steps.hint: An even group pairs with none left over. Look for the unpaired sock.
steps.explanation: Use pairing for odd/even, order for positions, and value for money.
steps.shortExplanation: Make, count or compare the objects. Explain what changed.

mathWorkshop.title: Partners, positions and coins
mathWorkshop.goal: Use pairing for odd/even, order for positions, and value for money.

tasks.prompt: Seven socks make three pairs and one left over. Is seven odd or even?
tasks.feedback: One sock has no partner, so seven is odd.
tasks.hint: An even group pairs with none left over. Look for the unpaired sock.

tasks.prompt: Ali finishes first, Mona second and Omar third. Who is in second position?
tasks.feedback: Mona is second: after Ali and before Omar.
tasks.hint: Second is the middle position in this three-person order.

tasks.prompt: One pound is one hundred piastres. Which coin is worth the most?
tasks.feedback: One pound is one hundred piastres, more than fifty or twenty-five.
tasks.hint: Compare the written values, rather than the number or size of coins.

parentReview.en: Guided practice is ungraded. Completion records the child doing the activities, not a book-question score.

steps.title: Even numbers
steps.hint: Can each number make pairs with none left over?
steps.explanation: 2, 8 and 14 make pairs with none left over.
steps.shortExplanation: 2, 8 and 14 make pairs with none left over.

steps.title: Odd or even
steps.hint: Pair up 7 things. Is one left alone?
steps.explanation: Seven makes three pairs and one left over, so it is odd.
steps.shortExplanation: Seven makes three pairs and one left over, so it is odd.

steps.title: Counting in twos
steps.prompt: Count in twos and fill the gaps.
steps.hint: Each number is two more than the one before.
steps.explanation: Counting in twos adds 2 each time.
steps.shortExplanation: Counting in twos adds 2 each time.

steps.title: Race positions
steps.prompt: Ali came 1st, Mona 2nd and Omar 3rd. Who came 2nd?
steps.hint: Who finished just after the one who came 1st?
steps.explanation: Mona is in the second position.
steps.shortExplanation: Mona is in the second position.

steps.title: Third from the left
steps.prompt: Which position means the third star from the left?
steps.hint: Touch the stars from the left: first, second, third.
steps.explanation: The third star from the left is in position 3rd.
steps.shortExplanation: The third star from the left is in position 3rd.

source.answerKeyText: The third star from the left.

steps.title: Parts of 14
steps.hint: What do you add to 10 to make 14? And to 7?

steps.title: Coin values
steps.prompt: Which coin is worth the most?
steps.hint: Read the value on each coin, not its size.
steps.explanation: One pound is 100 piastres, more than 50 or 25 piastres.
steps.shortExplanation: One pound is 100 piastres, more than 50 or 25 piastres.

steps.title: Pairs of socks
steps.prompt: You have 5 pairs of socks. How many socks?
steps.hint: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in twos.
steps.explanation: Each pair has 2 socks. Five pairs have 10 socks.
steps.shortExplanation: Each pair has 2 socks. Five pairs have 10 socks.

steps.title: What even means

options.label: pair up with none left over

steps.hint: Try pairing up 6 counters. Is any left over?
steps.explanation: Even numbers make pairs with none left over.
steps.shortExplanation: Even numbers make pairs with none left over.

source.answerKeyText: pair up with none left over

steps.title: An odd number
steps.hint: Pair up each number. Which one leaves one alone?
steps.explanation: 9 makes four pairs with one left over, so it is odd.
steps.shortExplanation: 9 makes four pairs with one left over, so it is odd.

steps.title: After 2nd
steps.hint: Say first, second, then the next position.

steps.title: Egyptian money
steps.hint: What are the coins and notes in Egypt called?
steps.explanation: In Egypt we pay with pounds and piastres.
steps.shortExplanation: In Egypt we pay with pounds and piastres.

steps.title: Making 12
steps.hint: Start at 10. How many more make 12?
steps.explanation: Ten and two more make twelve.
steps.shortExplanation: Ten and two more make twelve.

stickers.meaning: A number that makes pairs with one left over.

homeActivities.text: Pair socks to decide odd or even. Race three toy cars to name positions. Compare supervised coins by written value, not the number of coins.
homeActivities.textAr: حطّوا الشرابات أزواج عشان تعرفوا العدد فردي ولا زوجي. اعملوا سباق بـ ٣ عربيات لعب وقولوا مين الأول والتاني والتالت. وقارنوا الفلوس (مع حد كبير) بالقيمة المكتوبة عليها، مش بعدد العملات.
